title: Session Handoff
eyebrow: Design · picking up where the last session stopped

short.lead: Today, a session's work survives only if the agent remembers to commit, push and write a handoff note. The last handoff note (docs/handoff-2026-10-15.md) and docs/5-today/Today.md were both last written on 2026-10-15. Issue #140, which asks for a handoff document and a commit of everything at 95% usage, is still open. A different account shares nothing with the previous one except the git remote and, if it is on the same machine, the folder. So everything the next session needs has to be written into the repo and pushed while the work happens, not at the end. A usage limit can stop a session mid-turn, before any end-of-session step runs.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what it covers.
items: hook.py event_autosave already saves a subagent's work after each edit and pushes it, without touching the branch. Today it only runs on subagent worktree branches (the separate working folders subagents use).
The same mechanism is extended to the main session, so no second saving system is built.
docs/handoff-2026-10-15.md is the only one. It was written by hand and is now 24 days out of date.
Replaced by one file, docs/5-today/Handoff.md, that is rewritten every turn. The old note moves to docs/archive.
Asks for a handoff document and a commit of everything when usage reaches 95%.
Covered by saving continuously instead, so no usage threshold is needed. Issue #140 gets a comment pointing to this page.

After each file edit (at most once a minute), the whole working folder is saved as a snapshot and pushed to the remote under a separate name, refs/autosave/<branch>, that sits outside your branches. The snapshot includes files git is not tracking yet. Your branch, its history and the staging area are never changed.
The most work a sudden stop can lose is the last minute.
The handoff file, rewritten every turn

At the end of every turn, a hook writes docs/5-today/Handoff.md from facts it can read. Those facts are the branch, unpushed commits, unsaved files, the current stage of the design loop, open issues and their labels, your last request and the last recap. The file is saved with the snapshot.
Works even when the agent never gets to write anything itself.

Sometimes a turn changes files but leaves docs/5-today/Today.md alone. Then a check at the end of the turn asks the agent, once, to update Today.md and the section of docs/ that changed (the docs are split into tiers such as 5-today). This is the existing docs rule, now enforced instead of only reminded.

At session start, the plugin fetches the snapshot refs from the remote, reads the newest Handoff.md, and shows it at the top of the session. If a snapshot holds work that the folder does not, the plugin says so and offers to restore it.
Same account or not, same folder or a fresh clone, the next session starts from where the last stopped.
Whether a turn-end hook runs when a usage limit cuts a turn short
I have not yet checked this against Claude Code's documentation. This is why saving also happens after each edit, not only at the end of a turn.
I check this before building, and the answer goes on the build plan.

choices: q1
1. Where does the saved work go?
A
A snapshot pushed to refs/autosave/<branch>, outside your branch
Nothing lands on your branch or in its history, so the rule against finishing work you started holds on every branch, main included.
B
Work-in-progress commits straight onto the current branch
Easiest to find, but it fills the branch history with work-in-progress commits, and it cannot be used on main or on your own branches.
Either way the work is pushed, because a different account can only see what is on the remote.
q2
2. Who writes the handoff?
A
The hook writes the facts every turn; the agent adds a short plain summary when it can
The facts survive a sudden stop; the summary makes it readable.
B
The hook only, facts and no summary
Fully mechanical, but a reader has to piece together what was going on.
C
The agent only, asked at turn end
Most readable, but lost whenever the session is cut off.
q3
3. What should happen when saved work is found at session start?
A
Say what was found and ask before restoring it
Nothing in the folder is overwritten without your yes.
B
Restore it automatically
No question to answer, but it can overwrite something you changed by hand since.

wrapup.summary: A design for saving every session's work and handoff into the repo as it happens, so any next session can carry on.
wrapup.changing: Nothing yet. No code is written until you approve.
wrapup.blocking: Your pick of one option for each of the 3 questions above, or what you want changed.
